title: Product of Array Except Self
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`.

The product of any prefix or suffix of `nums` is guaranteed to fit in a **32-bit integer**.

You must solve it **without division** and in **O(n)** time.

Can you solve it using O(1) extra space (excluding the output array)? The key realization is that each position's result is the product of everything to its left times everything to its right.

examples.explanation: All positions except index 2 include a 0 factor, making the product 0.

editorial.approach: Use two passes over the array. In the first (left-to-right) pass, fill `answer[i]` with the product of all elements to the left of `i` (track a running `prefix` variable). In the second (right-to-left) pass, multiply each `answer[i]` by the product of all elements to its right (track a running `suffix` variable). This avoids division and uses only O(1) extra space, since the result array does not count toward the space complexity.
